item.title: Notre Dame vs Miami could deliver next legendary college football game
item.description: A college football game becomes truly legendary when it’s given a name. “The Miracle at Michigan,” “The Kick Six,” and “The Play” are all wonderful examples. One of the best “games with names” was actually slightly controversial – the legendary “Catholics vs. Convicts” game between Miami and Notre Dame in 1988. The nickname sprung from an unauthorized, unlicensed T-shirt made by Notre Dame students. The game was so legendary that ESPN made a “30 for 30” documentary about it. MORE: Biggest risers in College Football after Week 9 The game directly altered the course of the 1988 National Championship, as Notre Dame emerged victorious and went on to win it all. Fast forward to 2026. Notre Dame and Miami are slated to meet in Notre Dame Stadium on Saturday night. College Gameday will be there, and NBC will air the game nationally. It’s the Game of the Year, and the way we got here is feeling a lot like 1988. History could be repeating itself In that fateful 1988 matchup, the two teams entered with Miami ranking #1 and Notre Dame ranking #4 in the AP Poll. That’s precisely where the two teams enter this week. The 1988 game had direct National Championship implications, and this meet-up will have direct CFP implications. Both teams have plenty to prove Oct 31, 2026; Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; Miami (FL) Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates with tight end Gavin Mueller (87) after scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter at Kenan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The national media loves to discredit Notre Dame because of a perceived weak schedule, yet no one seems to do the same for Miami, when the schedules are more alike than different. Heading into Week 10, Notre Dame’s strength of schedule ranks 55th, and Miami 49th. Ironically, both teams had quite easy draws from the ACC. Notre Dame plays 5 ACC games per year, and this year, they drew Miami, SMU, and three below-average ACC opponents. USC canceling their rivalry game with Notre Dame didn’t help things, either. For Miami, they have already beaten Wake Forest, but do not draw Louisville or SMU. The simple fact of the matter is that, for both of these teams, weak schedules make this game matter more. We won’t get many more opportunities to see either of these teams against College Football Playoff-level competition. And a loss would be massively detrimental for both programs. For Notre Dame, we just saw a 10-2 Notre Dame team get denied entry to the CFP last season. For Miami, losing this game would create a razor-thin pathway. With no reputable wins outside of Wake Forest, Miami would likely need to win out and win the ACC Championship in order to qualify for the CFP. item.title: Carlos Eduardo Patetuci assesses Brazil U17's World Cup challenges
item.description: Carlos Eduardo Patetuci assesses Brazil U17's World Cup challenges Under-17 national team coach will use the preparation period to fine-tune the team Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF The Brazil men's Under-17 national team is in the final stages of preparation for the 2026 World Cup in Qatar. At Granja Comary in Teresópolis, Rio de Janeiro state, where the team will remain until November 14 before departing for the host country, coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci plans to use the training period to improve team chemistry, test different player combinations and prepare the squad for the challenges of the competition. “We'll use the time we have to strengthen the players' understanding of one another, test different combinations and possible lineups, using various systems. The idea is to make the most of this period to practice the options we might need at the World Cup,” he explained. Patetuci also assessed the team's progress throughout the preparation cycle and highlighted the contribution of friendlies and international tournaments. In his view, facing national teams from different continents helped the squad become familiar with other footballing styles and broaden its repertoire. Participation in the UEFA tournament held last month in Switzerland ( look back here ) was singled out as an important experience. Brazil faced Spain and Côte d'Ivoire, opponents with different characteristics from those of South American national teams. “It was very important to face these teams so close to the World Cup. It allowed us to experience other footballing cultures. African teams have a very strong physical element, but they are also improving technically and looking to play with more combinations. European teams, meanwhile, play a more organized style of football. We use drills that replicate these characteristics so we are ready for those kinds of matchups,” he said. The coach also noted that many of the players called up for the World Cup took part in the tournament in Switzerland, making it easier to maintain continuity and prepare for their group-stage opponents. Patetuci stressed that Brazil enters every competition committed to winning matches and lifting the trophy. At the same time, he believes international experience is part of the development process for players who are still growing at the age of 17. “When it comes to the Brazilian national team, we must always think about winning and claiming titles. That is our priority. But we know that player development happens at the same time. Every call-up, friendly and official competition is part of that process. We aim to win, but we also understand that the players are developing with every match and every tournament,” he reflected. item.title: Trey Nyoni Reportedly Set to Sign New Long-Term Liverpool Contract
item.description: Heading into the 2026-27 season, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola looked to have been a lack of options in midfield that had plenty on the outside feeling nervous. There was some hope, though—nervous, cautious, but hope—around young Trey Nyoni. Liverpool had signed him as a 16-year-old from Leicester City, eventually paying a fee of around £1M set by tribunal after the two cubs couldn’t agree compensation, and he was widely seen as a highly promising prospect. Promise, though, is a long way from the now 19-year-old being expected to be a difference maker. That’s exactly what he’s been, though, with the midfielder having started the club’s last two games and on pace to record close to 2,000 minutes of first team action this season. Nyoni is also reportedly in line for a new contract, with the player said to be close to agreeing a new long-term deal with the club as Liverpool push to ensure his long-term future is in Red. Last summer saw Nottingham Forest test Liverpool’s belief in Nyoni when they floated a £30M offer for the England youth international, but that approach was rebuffed instantly with Liverpool signalling they saw Nyoni as a key part of their future plans.

item.title: Casey, Jansen and Timoney start against Argentina
item.description: Ireland resume their Nations Championship campaign against Argentina in Dublin on Friday night [Getty Images] Nick Timoney, Craig Casey and Sean Jansen will start for Ireland against Argentina in the Nations Championship on Friday night, with Jamison Gibson Park and Josh van der Flier on the bench at the Aviva Stadium. With captain Caelan Doris and two-tour British and Irish Lion Jack Conan missing through injury, Connacht's Jansen always seemed the most likely to fill in at number eight for head coach Andy Farrell. The 27-year-old made a try-scoring debut for Ireland against Japan in July and followed that with a cameo as a replacement against the All Blacks a week later. The selections of Casey and Timoney, however, were less expected. Influential scrum-half Gibson-Park has arguably been Ireland's best performer in recent seasons. The 34-year-old missed the start of Leinster's season with a groin injury but made his return in the win over Munster on 24 October. With only that game under his belt this season, he will start on the bench with Casey preferred to start at nine in a half-back partnership with fly-half Sam Prendergast, who has recovered from a wrist injury. Ulster back row Timoney, 31, previously struggled to regularly break into the side despite strong form for his province but selection against Argentina means he will be involved in his ninth consecutive Test. Seven of those, however, have been from the bench and his start on Friday night comes at the expense of former World Rugby Player of the Year Van der Flier. With Garry Ringrose ruled out because of a hamstring problem, the experienced Robbie Henshaw will wear the 13 jersey, forming a midfield partnership with Stuart McCloskey. Wing Mack Hansen, prop Andrew Porter and Ryan Baird all start having not featured for Ireland since the defeat by South Africa in November 2025. All three missed both the Six Nations and summer fixtures in the Nations Championship through injury. Hansen starts in the number 11 jersey in what is Ireland's first home game since James Lowe's departure from Irish rugby, with Robert Baloucoune keeping his spot on the right wing and Hugo Keenan selected at full-back. Baird is selected at blind-side flanker, joining Timoney and Jansen in the back row. Porter's return at loose-head will be a considerable boost for Andy Farrell after recent windows were impact by injury problems at the position. He will pack down alongside hooker Dan Sheehan, who captains the side in Doris' absence, and tight-head Tadhg Furlong. Furlong is free to play after he was cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin last month. With Tadhg Beirne and Joe McCarthy selected as starting locks, James Ryan must make do with a place on the bench alongside Van der Flier and Gibson-Park. item.title: Filipe Luís on Monaco’s Folarin Balogun: ‘He’s been through a lot since the World Cup. His form in training has improved a lot.’
item.description: Filipe Luís on Monaco’s Folarin Balogun: ‘He’s been through a lot since the World Cup. His form in training has improved a lot.’ Folarin Balogun (25) is back in the team and back on the scoresheet. The USMNT forward returned from the FIFA World Cup injured, whilst his aborted move to Everton on transfer deadline day was a considerable distraction. That came after, if not the most prolific, at least the most complete season of his career. He netted 19 goals in 43 games in all competitions for the Principality club, but it was his link-up and work off the ball that also earned him plaudits. Balogun drafted into Monaco’s Conference League squad Due to his knee injury, he missed the start of the season and was subsequently omitted from Monaco’s UEFA Conference League squad. On Sunday, in a 3-1 loss to Paris FC, he netted his first goal since returning. On Tuesday, the USMNT international replaced the injured Ansu Fati in Monaco’s Conference League squad. He will therefore be eligible to face Nordsjaelland on Thursday night. Speaking at a press conference attended by Get French Football News, Filipe Luís addressed Balogun’s return: “I think it’s important for Balogun also [to come into the Conference League squad]. He’s been training fantastically in the last couple of weeks. I can see that his form in training has improved a lot. And you all know he’s a top player. And we want to get the best of him. So in this case, I think having the Conference League, also to give minutes and get this feeling back of being a football player, a Monaco player, is going to help him regain his form, but also help the team with what we need. So this is very important for us. And it’s going to be good to see him on the pitch. ‘It’s very good to have Balogun back’ – Luís “ For sure, what he lives, since the World Cup has not been normal for him. He’s been through a lot since the World Cup, the transfer window and everything. So sometimes some players are really fast, but sometimes players take a little bit longer. But as I said, in the last couple of weeks, he’s been fantastic in training. And of course, you can see that. You can see it. The players see it. The coach sees it. And when the players are like this, it is natural that he gets minutes to play. “ Of course, he’s a player who generates a lot for himself. He’s very dangerous attacking the space. He’s very strong. Shoot with both legs. Have this feeling that he wants to score goals. And yeah, it’s very good to have him back. “ GFFN | Luke Entwistle – reporting from Monaco

item.title: North Central Michigan women's cross country makes program history
item.description: PETOSKEY — The North Central Michigan College athletic program is still young. So, history-making moments are more than likely still going to come each season. But, the NCMC women’s cross country team just made the kind that stands out in any program and is sure to leave a lasting mark. The Timberwolves’ women’s cross country team became the first NCMC athletic team to make a national championship when they recently qualified for the NJCAA DII National Championships. After finishing runner-up in the Michigan Community College Athletic Association championships, the Timberwolves turned in a fifth place finish out of 12 teams in the MCCAA/Region XII Championships at Goodells County Park in St. Clair. The finish comes a year after the NCMC women’s team placed 11th in the region championship race, highlighting their leap in one season for a completely new team made up of all freshmen. The NJCAA DII National Championships will take place on Saturday, Nov. 14 in Huntsville, Ala. Cross Country Regionals: Seven area teams, nine other runners earn way to cross country state finals Muskegon Community College earned the regional title behind a 63-point finish, followed closely by Grand Rapids Community College with 69 points. Macomb then placed third with 93, St. Clair County was fourth with 128, followed then by North Central’s 154. On top of the team finish for NCMC, Esther Hornibrook set a new program record for a 5K race. Hornibrook, who grew up home schooled in Petoskey, ran an eighth place time of 19 minutes, 45.5 seconds. North Central’s Sahara Davis (Reed City) then followed in 27th (21:12.8), Teryn Firack (Pickford) placed 30th (21:22.2) and Makayla Watkins (Reed City) took 44th (22:09.6). item.title: Detroit Tigers Could Receive Surprise First-Round Draft Pick Thanks to Kevin McGonigle
item.description: The Detroit Tigers could be just days away from receiving an unexpected bonus that would make Kevin McGonigle’s remarkable rookie season even more valuable. If McGonigle wins the 2026 American League Rookie of the Year Award, Detroit will receive an additional selection at the end of the first round of the 2027 MLB Draft. That’s right. One more award for McGonigle could mean another premium prospect entering the Tigers’ farm system. And for an organization looking to bounce back from a disappointing 2026 season, that’s a pretty significant development. Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle (7) prepares to bat against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park in Detroit on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kevin McGonigle Could Earn Tigers an Extra First-Round Pick On Monday, McGonigle was officially named one of three finalists for the American League Rookie of the Year Award, joining Cleveland Guardians pitcher Parker Messick and Boston Red Sox left-hander Payton Tolle. According to the official announcement of the finalists , the winner will be revealed on Monday, November 9, at 7 p.m. ET on MLB Network. But there’s much more at stake than the trophy. Thanks to MLB’s Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI) program, teams can earn an additional draft selection when an eligible top prospect begins the season on the major league roster and achieves certain award-related milestones. McGonigle checks the necessary eligibility boxes, meaning Detroit would receive a selection at the end of the first round if he takes home the Baseball Writers’ Association of America award. The program was established as part of the 2022 collective bargaining agreement to encourage organizations to promote their best young players rather than delay their major league debuts for service-time considerations. That could turn out to be an enormous bonus for Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris. McGonigle’s Incredible Rookie Season Has Him in Position The 22-year-old infielder certainly has the numbers to make a compelling case. McGonigle finished the 2026 season with a .278 batting average, 18 home runs, 72 RBIs, 97 runs scored, 168 hits, 95 walks, and an impressive .806 OPS. Even more remarkable, his 7.1 Baseball-Reference WAR led every player in the American League. As we previously reported when McGonigle won The Sporting News AL Rookie of the Year Award , he has already received major recognition for his historic debut season. McGonigle also earned the Players Choice Award for AL Outstanding Rookie, adding to his growing collection of honors. And now, he’s one victory away from potentially adding an extra draft asset to Detroit’s future. Why This Would Be Huge for the Detroit Tigers Here’s where things get particularly interesting. item.title: FGCU women's basketball team falls in season-opener at Indiana
item.description: FGCU women’s basketball fell in its season-opener on Tuesday night, Nov. 3, losing 79-50 to Indiana at the Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall in Bloomington, Indiana. The Hoosiers led from the start, opening an 8-0 run through the first five minutes of the game and never looked back. The hosts outscored the Eagles 19-5 in the first quarter and while their offense picked up in the second, the Eagles couldn’t cut into the deficit by halftime. But just as the Eagles thought they had found their footing, Indiana shifted gears in the third quarter, going on a 17-0 run to break the game wide open. Junior forward Zania Socka-Nguemen led the Hoosiers with 13 points and seven rebounds while senior forward Alisa Williams had 12 points off the bench as the Hoosiers cruised to a lopsided victory. Junior guard Sinai Douglas led the Eagles with 13 points and senior guard Denika Lightbourne provided support with 10 points. The Eagles shooting struggles continued throughout the night, shooting just 29% from the field as a team and making only 3 of their 26 3-point attempts. FGCU (0-1) will look to bounce back when the Eagles return to Alico Arena for their home-opener against Arkansas State on Saturday, Nov. 7 at 2 p.m. This article originally appeared on Naples Daily News: FGCU women's basketball team falls in season-opener at Indiana

item.title: Red Sox Predicted To Replace Sonny Gray With 4.32 ERA All-Star
item.description: San Diego Padres pitcher Casey Mize Sonny Gray is a free agent, and the Boston Red Sox may need to replace him. There is no shortage of pitchers on the open market, but there is a shortage of quality ones. Tarik Skubal, Michael King and Freddy Peralta are the best options, but there is a falloff after that. Bleacher Report predicted the Red Sox would sign Casey Mize to replace Gray. "Mize could replace Sonny Gray in Boston's rotation on a one-year commitment," wrote Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly. "If he stays healthy and pitches well, he could be a qualifying-offer candidate next year." Mize had a 4.23 ERA last season and has a lengthy injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in 2022. He has also had a procedure done on his back. Last season, he had an adductor strain and an ankle sprain that required stints on the injured list. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Mize was one of the most sought-after players at the trade deadline, posting a 2.70 ERA in 16 starts with the Detroit Tigers. The Padres got him, but he had a 7.46 ERA with them. He did not pitch in the postseason, and certainly cost himself some money. However, Kelly predicted he would sign a one-year, $14 million deal to join the Red Sox. That type of deal is not very risky for the Red Sox, and he could be a solid No. 5 starter. Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suarez and Jake Bennett should make for a solid top four, and Mize could slot in as No. 5. He has been an All-Star in the past, and the hope would be that he can return to that form for the Red Sox. More MLB: Another Rafael Devers Trade Not Out of Question This Offseason

(Photo by Keith Gillett/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s time to declare the 2026 Iowa Football team as the Jekyll and Hyde Hawkeyes. I have no clue what to think of this team, and I have no clue what version of the team is going to show up on any given Saturday. When they’re good, they’re really good, and when they’re bad, woof, they’re really bad. The fate of the program’s hope for a playoff appearance this season now rides on this weekend’s trip to Evanston for a huge matchup against -checks notes- -checks notes again- the Northwestern Wildcats, who are having a breakout season in head coach David Braun’s fourth season at the helm of the program. The Wildcats are a talented team and Iowa will have its hands full, particularly if the Hyde version makes its appearance on the road once again, under the lights at Northwestern’s incredible looking new stadium. But let’s not focus on what I think, let’s see what Kirk Ferentz had to say about things in his weekly press conference, shall we? Check out the full transcript HERE and my highlights and snark below. -snort- We’ll start with this, something bigger than football: KIRK FERENTZ: Good afternoon. So, a little bit last weekend and move on to this game coming up. You know, with Jack Campbell, we all became aware on Sunday shortly after what was going on there, and I want to share our support certainly to the family and, most importantly, to Jack. Been in contact with the family, expressed that to them, and they’ve kept us updated, but we’re going to respect their wishes right now. They’ll handle the information that comes out. When they think it’s appropriate, they’ll release that information and go from there. I think all of you know just how impactful Jack was in our program, what a tremendous person he is, what a tremendous player he’s been for us, and now he’s moved on and done the exact same thing in Detroit. item.title: ‘Never seen anything like it’ – Stephen A. Smith says NBA player is stealing a living
item.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Stephen A. Smith has officially reached his breaking point with NBA injury absences. The NBA’s injury bug has gotten completely out of hand, and fans are frankly tired of checking injury reports just to see if a game is worth turning on. Night after night, the best matchups go missing as guys like Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Haliburton find themselves sidelined. Even LeBron chimed in, admitting the level of conditioning guys need just to survive today’s speed is crazy. The problem is so obvious that Adam Silver is actually floating 40-minute games to keep players in one piece. But shaving off a few minutes won’t magically solve how punishing this game has gotten. Stephen A. Smith accuses Kawhi Leonard of checking out Taking to his YouTube show , Stephen A. Smith went completely off on Kawhi Leonard . He’s clearly fed up with Kawhi living on the injury report, looking straight into the camera and insisting the Raptors star is robbing the franchise by pocketing hundreds of millions while barely seeing the floor. He said: “If he heard about an injured list, he was going to make sure he’s on it. If he heard about it, he was going to make sure he’s on it. So, we knew he was going to be on it. Now, the excuse this time is swelling in his left knee. I know it’s legit. I’m not accusing him of faking it. I’m just saying perpetually there’s always some injury with him. I’m telling y’all right now. “The man is an absolute pro of getting paid without working. I’ve never seen anything like it in my life. I’ve never seen anything like it ever. It’s just unbelievable. I want him to give classes on that. This guy is something special. How do I get paid without working? Kawhi Leonard. That’s all you got to name the class.” Kawhi actually made his return debut for Toronto in late October, only for his knee to flare up immediately after. It’s the exact same nightmare that plagued him with the Spurs and Clippers. He’s unbelievable when healthy, but forever betrayed by chronic inflammation and surgeries that keep him sidelined. item.description: Bronson Hearn-Smith won gold in the 200m at July's European U18 Championships, setting a new championship record time of 20.70 in the final [Getty Images] Teenage sprinter Bronson Hearn-Smith said he would try his "absolute hardest" to qualify for the 2028 Olympic Games after he was accepted onto a talent scheme targeted at future medal hopefuls. The 16-year-old from Tiptree, Essex, won European Under-18 gold in the 200m in July, setting a new championship record time of 20.70 secs in the final. Last month he signed with Matchroom's Talent Agency and has now secured a place on UK Athletics' Olympic Futures and Futures Relay Sprint programmes. "I'm so grateful to be a part of it. It's a big honour and I'm so excited to be joining." he told BBC Essex. "I'd love to go to the Olympics, I would. Fingers crossed obviously, touch wood as well, nothing is certain. "I'm going to try my absolute hardest. If I make the relay team then that's an achievement in itself and I'd say that is as big as doing an individual competition there." Even before his European success, Hearn-Smith, of Colchester Harriers Athletics Club, had attracted a large social media following. Clips of his seemingly effortless running style, characterised by long strides, have attracted millions of views on platforms including TikTok and YouTube. He said: "I've just been doing what I've been doing for like three years. Honestly there's been no change in training regime it's all been working in my favour and I'm just going to carry on with that because I'm getting that bit quicker. item.title: Ex-Liverpool and Chelsea full-back Glen Johnson backs Anfield as better fit for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott amid £100m transfer battle
item.description: Arsenal v Bournemouth - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Former England right-back Glen Johnson has urged Bournemouth playmaker Alex Scott to snub Chelsea in favour of joining Liverpool during the upcoming January transfer window. Both Premier League heavyweights are competing to sign the 23-year-old midfielder after the south coast club set a £100 million asking price for their prized asset. Former defender advises England midfielder Johnson believes the calmer environment on Merseyside makes Anfield the ideal destination for the former Bristol City talent compared to Stamford Bridge. Both clubs have tracked the England international closely since he moved to the Vitality Stadium for £25m in 2023. item.title: Why LIV Golf’s collapse could be a boon for this European country
item.description: Four years after LIV Golf turned the men’s professional game upside down, the question is no longer which stars it might lure away with Saudi riches, but whether the breakaway circuit can keep enough of them to survive. After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, LIV is now trying to secure enough players and financial backing to launch a revamped version of the competition in 2027. That task has become harder as a stream of prominent players head for the exit. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter have all said their farewells. For Scotland, this is more than distant turmoil: LIV players have become a significant presence at the Genesis Scottish Open and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship , raising the question of what their changing allegiances could mean for two of the country’s biggest tournaments. So where does LIV stand now? Its proposed new financial backer, BC Partners, has lined up a potential funding package of up to $300 million aimed at keeping the league running. But the investor wants what has been described as a “critical mass” of players to commit to the new competition. And that is the problem. Some of LIV’s most recognisable names have already decided against the new venture. Rahm has provided the biggest blow, with his lawyer telling the bankruptcy court that the Spaniard regarded the terms offered for LIV 2.0 as unacceptable. Other departures have gathered pace, while Bryson DeChambeau, one of LIV’s most valuable remaining attractions, has yet to make a public commitment to LIV 2.0. What has any of that got to do with Scotland? Potentially quite a lot. Seven LIV players competed in July’s Genesis Scottish Open at the Renaissance Club in East Lothian , including Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Tom McKibbin, Meronk, Puig, Victor Perez and Laurie Canter. The loss dropped Miami to 2-5, but the bigger concern is how frequently the same problems continue to surface. The Heat have allowed at least 125 points in five of their first seven games, with a defensive rating of 119.8 that ranks 27th in the league. Opponents are also shooting 41% from beyond the arc against Miami, one of the highest marks in the NBA. A slow start can be corrected. A shooting slump can pass. However, when the defense consistently struggles, the problems tend to run much deeper, especially with an increasingly challenging November schedule for the Heat ahead . If Miami cannot find answers defensively, things could get even more difficult as the season progresses. For Miami, the concern is no longer just about individual matchups or missed rotations. The Heat are struggling to defend as a team, threatening one of the biggest reasons they have remained competitive over the years. Perimeter defenders need help when opponents get past the initial point of attack, while big men need teammates to rotate and recover.
